test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Mar 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following schedules of the Constitution of India has to be amended for the formation of a new state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**First Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The First Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists all the states and union territories along with their territories.
 
• Any changes in the boundaries, names, or formation of new states or union territories require an amendment to the First Schedule.
 
• The formation of a new state involves the reorganization of existing states or union territories, which must be reflected in the First Schedule.
 
• Amending the First Schedule requires a constitutional amendment, which must be passed by both houses of Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fourth Schedule:**

 
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• It specifies the number of seats allocated to each state and union territory.
 
• Changes to this schedule do not relate to the formation of new states but to the representation in the Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Third Schedule:**
 
 
• The Third Schedule lists the forms of oaths or affirmations for various constitutional posts, including the President, judges, and members of Parliament and state legislatures.
 
• This schedule is not related to the formation of new states.
 
 
 
• **Second Schedule:**
 
 
• The Second Schedule of the Constitution deals with the emoluments, allowances, and privileges of various constitutional office holders like the President, Governors, Judges, etc.
 
• It does not pertain to the formation of new states.
